_omitted_from_the_page.model_version: The engine's deployed API carries the version 1.0.0, set once when the service was created and never moved. It is a deployment string, not a version of the model, so publishing it as one would say something untrue.

safety_checks.name: Hard medication conflict
safety_checks.does: Removes products that cannot be taken alongside a medication the customer says they are on.

safety_checks.name: Declared medication caution
safety_checks.does: Adds a warning to products whose own label cautions against a medication the customer is on, and removes nothing.

safety_checks.name: Diagnosed condition conflict
safety_checks.does: Removes products that the product record says to avoid with a condition the customer has told us about.

safety_checks.name: Pregnancy and breastfeeding safety
safety_checks.does: Removes products that are not safe in pregnancy or while breastfeeding.

safety_checks.name: Prenatal audience only
safety_checks.does: Removes products meant only for people trying to conceive, pregnant or breastfeeding from everybody else's plan.

safety_checks.name: Sex-specific products
safety_checks.does: Removes products formulated for one sex from the other sex's plan.

safety_checks.name: Beta-carotene for smokers
safety_checks.does: Removes products that raise risk for current smokers, beta-carotene above all.

safety_checks.name: Age band suitability
safety_checks.does: Removes products with no established requirement or dose for the customer's age and sex.

safety_checks.name: Iron need check
safety_checks.does: Removes standalone iron from plans for people whose physiological need for it is low, because unneeded iron is not benign.

safety_checks.name: Low body weight safety
safety_checks.does: Removes products that are unsafe or inappropriate at a very low body weight, and signposts support instead.

safety_checks.name: Training-only products
safety_checks.does: Removes sport and training products from the plan of somebody who reports no structured exercise.

safety_checks.name: Stimulants against sleep
safety_checks.does: Removes caffeine-bearing products when the customer's goal is better sleep, or when they already sleep six hours or fewer.

safety_checks.name: Total caffeine ceiling
safety_checks.does: Removes caffeine-bearing products once the total caffeine across the whole plan would pass the daily ceiling.

safety_checks.name: No reference intake ceiling
safety_checks.does: Removes single-nutrient products for nutrients with no established reference intake, where no real shortfall can be shown.

safety_checks.name: Tolerable upper limit
safety_checks.does: Removes any product whose serving would take the customer's total intake of a nutrient past its tolerable upper limit.

safety_checks.name: Diet compatibility
safety_checks.does: Removes products that clash with the customer's diet, in both directions: incompatible ingredients, and vegan alternatives offered to somebody who is not vegan.

safety_checks.name: Market ingredient legality
safety_checks.does: Removes products containing an ingredient that cannot legally be sold as a food supplement in the customer's market.

plan_checks.name: One multivitamin only
plan_checks.does: Removes every multivitamin after the best-matching one.

plan_checks.name: Multivitamin against standalone
plan_checks.does: Removes a single-nutrient product when a recommended multivitamin already supplies that nutrient.

plan_checks.name: One per product family
plan_checks.does: Removes products from a family where taking more than one together adds nothing, keeping the best match.

plan_checks.name: Duplicate active ingredient
plan_checks.does: Removes a product whose active ingredient is already covered by another product in the plan.

plan_checks.name: Redundant complex
plan_checks.does: Removes a combination product whose contents are already covered by the single-nutrient products in the plan.

plan_checks.name: Already met by diet
plan_checks.does: Removes a product for a nutrient the customer's own food intake already supplies at or above their target.

also_in_the_chain.note: Classified so the two published figures above can be shown to be complete rather than merely short. Neither the safety count nor the plan count includes these.

claim_compliance.name: Authorised claim required
claim_compliance.does: Demotes botanical products when nothing in the set carries an authorised health claim for what the customer asked about.

claim_compliance.name: Goal claim authorisation
claim_compliance.does: Demotes a product whose only reason to be in the plan is a claim that is not authorised.

claim_compliance.name: Symptom claim authorisation
claim_compliance.does: Stops a product being presented against a specific symptom it holds no authorised claim for.

advisory_notices.name: Additive medication risk
advisory_notices.does: Adds a warning where a product and a medication carry an additive risk that is real but not absolute.

advisory_notices.name: Zinc and copper balance
advisory_notices.does: Adds a warning when zinc is recommended at a level that can deplete copper without paired copper.

advisory_notices.name: Missing bone cofactors
advisory_notices.does: Adds a note when vitamin D is recommended without the cofactors that help it work.

advisory_notices.name: No safe dose available
advisory_notices.does: Adds a note when a shortfall is found but the brand carries no product that could fill it at a safe dose.

advisory_notices.name: Expert supervision advised
advisory_notices.does: Marks products that should never be presented as a straightforward buy, whatever the customer's answers.

advisory_notices.name: Pregnancy referral note
advisory_notices.does: Marks products whose use in pregnancy is unestablished rather than unsafe, and refers the customer to a professional.

advisory_notices.name: No endorsement note
advisory_notices.does: Attaches the no-endorsement note to products that require one.

recommendation_thresholds.reference_adult: woman aged 31 to 50, non-smoker, lightly active, no dietary restriction
recommendation_thresholds.note: Shortfall is how far below target a nutrient must fall before a product is recommended for it. It sits on top of the upper limit, which refuses any dose that would breach a tolerable intake.

summary: Blend works out what you already get from food before it considers a supplement: your answers about meal pattern, portion size, how often you skip meals and how often you eat each food group are turned into an estimated daily plate in grams, and each food group's composition comes from a published food composition database.

That plate gives an estimated daily intake for every nutrient the model tracks, which is then set against your own personal target, so a nutrient your diet already covers reads as met rather than as a gap.
Where your food already supplies a nutrient at or above your own target, the supplement for it is removed from the plan instead of being recommended.

food_composition.coverage_note: Of 1276 food rows, 1218 matched the source's fatty-acid tables and 454 carry a measured value for both EPA and DHA. Where the source did not analyse the breakdown, the engine estimates the EPA and DHA share of total omega-3 by food group rather than treating the gap as zero.

fortification.why: Fortification is national law rather than composition: the United Kingdom requires calcium, iron, thiamin and niacin in non-wholemeal wheat flour and Denmark requires none, while the composition table is Danish.

credited_against_targets.how: Every nutrient's gap is the customer's own target minus their estimated intake from food, so the diet is credited against the target before any product is considered.
credited_against_targets.already_met_by_diet: A second check removes a product outright when the customer's food intake of that nutrient reaches their own displayed target. It uses the customer's own target rather than a fixed reference figure, so the plan can never recommend a product for a nutrient the report shows as met.

countries.market_varying_note: Nutrients with a per-market reference value in the overlays. The rest take the same target in every market.
countries.summary: Three reference sets cover every market the engine runs today. The United Kingdom and the European Union each have their own; the United States and Canada share one, because the Dietary Reference Intakes are a joint set.
countries.how_a_market_is_decided: The customer's own country decides, and the brand's home market fills the gap when it is unknown. A country with no reference set of its own falls back to its region, and anything that resolves to nothing at all is judged against the United Kingdom.
what_is_not_per_country: The shortfall a nutrient must show before a product is offered is one set of bands worldwide.
The tolerable upper limits are one set worldwide. The United Kingdom's own guidance on retinol, for one, is lower than the limit applied here.
Food composition is one table worldwide, with a fortification overlay for the United Kingdom only.
